title: easi-view: competitive feature catalog and phased roadmap
purpose: Browser-native DICOM viewer using EASI JS ingestion with an independently implemented rendering engine, loading runtime, tools, and workspace.
scope: A representative benchmark across 16 viewer/product families spanning browser, desktop, enterprise and advanced visualization. Documented capabilities inform the backlog; this is not an independently tested ranking or a promise of complete parity.

benchmarks.name: OHIF
benchmarks.focus: Configurable workflows, DICOMweb, measurements, segmentation, fusion, volume rendering and extensibility.
benchmarks.qualification: Pin a stable version for acceptance; current documentation also describes a beta branch.

benchmarks.name: Weasis
benchmarks.focus: Wide DICOM object coverage, presentation handling, quantitative tools, SEG/RT/ECG, MPR and 3D.
benchmarks.qualification: Web launch still requires installation; features must be checked against the selected release.

benchmarks.name: RadiAnt
benchmarks.focus: Fast everyday review, cine, comparative layouts, reconstruction and specialized analysis.
benchmarks.qualification: Installed and removable-media editions differ; some tools require add-ons or supported GPU hardware.

benchmarks.name: OsiriX MD
benchmarks.focus: Advanced workstation tools, reconstruction, registration, quantitative and specialty workflows.
benchmarks.qualification: Use MD as the benchmark; Lite and mobile products have different scope.

benchmarks.name: Horos
benchmarks.focus: Local organization, MPR, 3D, export and extensibility.
benchmarks.qualification: Project-authored evidence for some tools is historical; do not infer current parity from ancestry.

benchmarks.name: 3D Slicer
benchmarks.focus: Segmentation editing, quantitative analysis, registration, sequences and extension-based tools.
benchmarks.qualification: SlicerRT and other specialty packages are separate extensions; research features need their own intended-use validation.

benchmarks.name: MedDream
benchmarks.deployment: HTML5 browser viewer with archive integration
benchmarks.focus: General browser review, reconstruction, measurements, derived objects and specialty tools.
benchmarks.qualification: Capabilities depend on edition, archive configuration and separately licensed modules.

benchmarks.name: Visage 7
benchmarks.deployment: Native smart client with server processing/rendering
benchmarks.focus: Enterprise reading performance, prior studies and specialist diagnostic workflows.
benchmarks.qualification: Its desktop diagnostic architecture is not a browser-only zero-footprint viewer.

benchmarks.name: Sectra UniView / IDS7
benchmarks.deployment: UniView browser review plus IDS7 diagnostic application
benchmarks.focus: Enterprise access, reporting, collaboration, worklists, breast imaging and pathology.
benchmarks.qualification: Separate the browser review product from the richer diagnostic workstation and optional reporting/specialty contracts.

benchmarks.name: MicroDicom
benchmarks.focus: Compact desktop workflow, MPR/3D, fusion, tag editing, anonymization and DICOM/media export.
benchmarks.qualification: Current manual scope is broader than basic 2D. Portable native media is not browser-only.

benchmarks.name: DWV
benchmarks.focus: Local/remote loading, browser rendering, annotations and embeddable APIs.
benchmarks.qualification: Use its explicit stable conformance matrix; implementations and planned sections differ. GPL-3.0 is a separate dependency decision.

benchmarks.name: Intelerad InteleViewer / InteleConnect EV
benchmarks.deployment: Native workstation plus distinct browser portal
benchmarks.focus: Streaming diagnostic review, archive workflow and enterprise image access.
benchmarks.qualification: InteleViewer is a native Windows/macOS client; InteleConnect EV is the separate zero-footprint clinical portal.

benchmarks.name: Siemens syngo.via
benchmarks.focus: Quantitative specialty applications, background postprocessing, anatomical alignment and advanced visualization.
benchmarks.qualification: Application availability varies by license and country; standalone View&GO requires installation.

benchmarks.name: GE AW / Universal Viewer
benchmarks.deployment: Advanced thin-client platform plus separate enterprise viewers
benchmarks.focus: Server-assisted advanced visualization, neuro perfusion, specialized acquisition workflows and PACS integration.
benchmarks.qualification: Universal Viewer Zero Footprint is distinct from the broader AW application portfolio.

benchmarks.name: Philips Advanced Visualization Workspace
benchmarks.deployment: Advanced visualization platform with a modular application catalog
benchmarks.focus: Quantitative MRI/CT, perfusion, spectroscopy, liver/lung/neuro analysis and anatomical modeling.
benchmarks.qualification: The catalog includes a Zero Footprint Viewer as one app, plus licensed/third-party/country-dependent specialty applications.

benchmarks.name: TeraRecon AV / Intuition
benchmarks.focus: Cardiac/vascular intervention planning, specialty quantification, 3D and separate AI orchestration.
benchmarks.qualification: Preprocessing, optional applications, device libraries and backend products are separate capabilities.

architecture.responsibility: Transport and streaming DICOM parsing through the published pipeline APIs. Maintain the independently licensed library boundary.

architecture.component: EASI View frame source and runtime
architecture.responsibility: Normalized raw samples and geometry, lazy worker decoding, request cancellation, encoded input limits and byte-budgeted decoded caches.
Direct WebGL2 scalar textures and shaders, DICOM display transforms, calibrated coordinates and a CPU reference/fallback. Later own MPR and GPU volume rendering.
Framework-free ES-module 2D alpha, viewport interactions, calibrated measurements, cine, import and source lifecycle; later multi-viewport and extension APIs.
DICOMweb archives, identity provider, annotation/report persistence and Node DIMSE gateway. Local files remain in the browser.

principles: Zero-footprint means no installed viewer or browser plugin. Browser processing and server-backed archive/integration modes can coexist.
Local-file mode parses and displays locally, with no file upload or persistent patient-data storage by default.
EASI remains the ingest and normalization boundary through a direct raw-frame source contract.
Keep raw scalar samples and physical geometry; display RGBA is a presentation product, not a quantitative volume source.
Measure streaming value using time to first useful image, responsiveness, retained bytes, cancellation and buffer disposal.
Streaming already exists in other viewers. Differentiate through the expressive pipeline API, a reusable owned engine, resource control and integration experience.
Publish a capability matrix by SOP class, transfer syntax, photometric profile, frame model, browser/device and supported operations.
Clinical intended use, specialty algorithms and diagnostic measurements need explicit validation criteria separate from a feature checkbox.
Own the viewer engine, cache, and tools. Add codec-only providers deliberately; do not add a substantial third-party viewer or rendering framework.

phases.name: Owned engine and correctness foundation
phases.deliverables: Independent repository, matching source-available license, raw-pixel/frame/geometry contract, owned WebGL2 renderer with CPU reference, worker lifecycle, synthetic fixtures and byte-budgeted caches.
phases.gate: Independent signedness, High Bit, endian, window, inversion, orientation, spacing and cancellation tests pass; repeated loads dispose CPU/GPU resources; no external viewer engine is present.

phases.name: Professional 2D alpha
phases.deliverables: Local files/folders, study and series organization, one configured DICOMweb archive, thumbnails, stack navigation, cine with declared timing, presets, pan/zoom/rotate/flip, layouts, metadata, keyboard/touch and calibrated basic measurements.
phases.gate: An independently encoded CT/MR/X-ray/US corpus works across the selected browser/device matrix. Local viewing is network-free and unsupported inputs fail clearly.

phases.name: Reliable general viewer
phases.deliverables: Validated compressed and enhanced profiles, patient-geometry sorting, workers, bounded caches and prefetch, authenticated archive integration, priors, linked views, layout presets, richer ROI tools, persistence and operational hardening.
phases.gate: Published compatibility matrix, reproducible performance budgets, quantitative reference checks, repeated-study cleanup, multiple archive implementations and source-appropriate security/access tests all pass.

phases.name: Volume and multimodality workbench
phases.deliverables: Verified volume assembly, axial/coronal/sagittal and oblique MPR, crosshairs, reference lines, slabs, MIP/MinIP/average projections, curved reconstructions, 3D rendering, geometry-aware fusion and selected registration.
phases.gate: Known phantoms verify geometry and reformat measurements. Nonuniform, mixed-orientation or nonmatching-frame-of-reference data receives defined handling.

phases.name: Interoperable results and research
phases.deliverables: SEG viewing/editing, SR measurement tracking, GSPS/KOS, parametric maps, AI result overlays, quantification, longitudinal research and standards-based export/save.
phases.gate: Output objects retain correct image/frame references and units and round-trip through independently implemented viewers and validators. AI display, editing and execution have separate contracts.

phases.name: Enterprise workflow
phases.deliverables: Identity and roles, worklists, assignment, hanging-protocol authoring, reporting, EMR/FHIR context, sharing/collaboration, audit, policy controls, deployment operations and optional legacy PACS gateway.
phases.gate: Authorization, session cleanup, audit and concurrency are exercised end-to-end in a representative institution integration. Local-only mode remains an explicit supported workflow.

phases.name: Specialty workstations
phases.deliverables: Breast/DBT/ABUS, echo/cardiac/vascular, nuclear oncology, RT review, dental/orthopedics, WSI pathology, ophthalmology and advanced research analysis.
phases.gate: Choose each specialty explicitly with domain expertise, independently validated numerical and interaction tests and the necessary dependencies. Modules can proceed in parallel once their core prerequisites are proven.

kickoff: Create an independent local easi-view repository with matching community licensing and a synthetic-only asset policy.
Keep a focused src/data, src/runtime, src/render, src/ui, test and docs structure; split packages only when a reusable boundary is proven.
Implement a direct raw-frame contract and owned WebGL2 renderer with independent scalar, windowing and geometry expectations.
Prove one viewport using local files and a bounded native DICOMweb multipart response with lazy worker decoding and explicit resource cleanup.
Expand compressed and enhanced support through independently validated providers and additive EASI APIs when needed.
Build archive browsing, multiple viewports and richer tools after the first numerical and lifecycle gates pass.
Use the evidence-linked catalog for further scope decisions; keep actual support recorded in STATUS.md.
knownEasiGaps: Current convenience decoders primarily produce display RGBA. Quantitative pixels and volume loading need a raw scalar output contract.
Native multiframe detection and encapsulated fragment/frame extraction need broader correctness coverage, including empty/basic/extended offset tables.
Enhanced shared/per-frame metadata and exact modality/VOI/presentation behavior need normalized, independently validated support.
JPEG2000, JPEG-LS and HTJ2K runtimes require explicit provision, supported-profile validation and licensing notices.
Streaming the parser and selecting attributes do not automatically provide a bounded, frame-oriented viewer cache or progressive decoded frames.
SEG/SR/PresentationState accessors do not by themselves implement object visualization, editing or interoperable save workflows.
scopeNotes: The catalog is a comprehensive candidate backlog for the named benchmarks, not an exhaustive inventory of every viewer, optional module or future release.
Vendor documentation is evidence of advertised capability, not proof of accuracy, interoperability, performance or installation-specific availability.
Specialty entries are a menu of potential modules, not a simultaneous first-release commitment.
Keep EASI JS and its license/versioning separate from viewer code; preserve third-party runtime licenses and notices.
An independent local research alpha starts P0/P1. The broader feature catalog remains a candidate backlog, and publication is a later release task.
implementationStatus: 0.1.0-alpha.0 starts the P0/P1 native-monochrome slice. The catalog is a backlog, not a list of implemented capabilities. See STATUS.md.
